name: Baasha
charge: Walking in the way of Jeroboam after being exalted out of the dust to destroy Jeroboam’s house
summary: Baasha conspired against Nadab the son of Jeroboam, killed him, and destroyed all the house of Jeroboam as Ahijah had foretold, then reigned twenty-four years walking in the same way of Jeroboam (1 Kings 15:27-34). He built Ramah to stop the people of the north from going over to Asa and the Lord (2 Chronicles 16:1). The word came by Jehu the son of Hanani that the Lord, who had lifted him out of the dust, would make his house like the house of Jeroboam, and it was fulfilled when Zimri killed his son Elah and all his kin (1 Kings 16:1-13).
offenseFull: Nadab the son of Jeroboam reigned two years and did evil, walking in the way and sin of his father. Baasha the son of Ahijah, of the house of Issachar, conspired against him and struck him down at Gibbethon, reigned in his place, and struck all the house of Jeroboam, leaving none that breathed, according to the word the Lord spoke by Ahijah the Shilonite, because of the sins by which Jeroboam made Israel to sin (1 Kings 15:25-30). The study notes mark it as the fulfilment, years later, of the judgment on Jeroboam’s descendants. Then he reigned twenty-four years in Tirzah and did evil in the sight of the Lord, walking in the way of Jeroboam and in the sin he made Israel commit (1 Kings 15:33-34). The pattern continues: each king who follows takes up the sin of the one before, and the same judgments keep coming.

He also made war on Judah. There was war between Asa and Baasha all their days, and Baasha came up and built Ramah to keep anyone from going out or coming in to Asa king of Judah (1 Kings 15:16-17). The study notes on Chronicles give the reason: tribes out of Israel had been turning their hearts back to the Most High and joining Asa, and Baasha was trying to stop the northern kingdom from coming down to Judah (2 Chronicles 16:1). Asa, instead of crying to the Most High as he had against Zerah, hired Benhadad of Syria with the treasures of the Lord’s house to break his league with Baasha; Benhadad struck the cities of Israel, and Baasha left off building Ramah (2 Chronicles 16:2-6).
judgmentFull: The word of the Lord came to Jehu the son of Hanani against Baasha: the Lord had exalted him out of the dust and made him prince over His people Israel, and he had walked in the way of Jeroboam and made Israel sin, provoking Him with their sins. Therefore He would take away the posterity of Baasha and make his house like the house of Jeroboam; the dogs would eat those of his who died in the city, and the birds those who died in the field (1 Kings 16:1-4). The same judgment falls because the same sin is repeated, just as descendants keep the pattern of their fathers though they saw the ruin it brought. The word came against him both for all the evil he did in walking like Jeroboam and because he killed him (1 Kings 16:7). Baasha died and was buried in Tirzah, and Elah his son reigned (1 Kings 16:6).

Elah reigned two years. His servant Zimri, captain of half his chariots, killed him while he was drunk in a steward’s house, and as soon as Zimri sat on the throne he killed all the house of Baasha, leaving not one male, nor his kinsfolk nor his friends, according to the word spoken by Jehu (1 Kings 16:8-12). It all came for the sins of Baasha and of Elah his son, who provoked the Lord God of Israel to anger with their vanities (1 Kings 16:13). Moses saw it in the spirit: Israel grew fat and kicked, forsook the God who made him, and provoked Him to jealousy with strange gods (Deuteronomy 32:15-21). A generation later the same sentence was pronounced on Ahab, that his house would be made like the house of Jeroboam and like the house of Baasha (1 Kings 21:22).

text.text: And Baasha the son of Ahijah, of the house of Issachar, conspired against him; and Baasha smote him at Gibbethon, which belonged to the Philistines; for Nadab and all Israel laid siege to Gibbethon.
Even in the third year of Asa king of Judah did Baasha slay him, and reigned in his stead.

And it came to pass, when he reigned, that he smote all the house of Jeroboam; he left not to Jeroboam any that breathed, until he had destroyed him, according unto the saying of the Lord, which he spake by his servant Ahijah the Shilonite:
Because of the sins of Jeroboam which he sinned, and which he made Israel sin, by his provocation wherewith he provoked the Lord God of Israel to anger.
Now the rest of the acts of Nadab, and all that he did, are they not written in the book of the chronicles of the kings of Israel?
And there was war between Asa and Baasha king of Israel all their days.
In the third year of Asa king of Judah began Baasha the son of Ahijah to reign over all Israel in Tirzah, twenty and four years.
And he did evil in the sight of the Lord, and walked in the way of Jeroboam, and in his sin wherewith he made Israel to sin.
In the six and thirtieth year of the reign of Asa Baasha king of Israel came up against Judah, and built Ramah, to the intent that he might let none go out or come in to Asa king of Judah.
Then the word of the Lord came to Jehu the son of Hanani against Baasha, saying,

Forasmuch as I exalted thee out of the dust, and made thee prince over my people Israel; and thou hast walked in the way of Jeroboam, and hast made my people Israel to sin, to provoke me to anger with their sins;
Behold, I will take away the posterity of Baasha, and the posterity of his house; and will make thy house like the house of Jeroboam the son of Nebat.
Him that dieth of Baasha in the city shall the dogs eat; and him that dieth of his in the fields shall the fowls of the air eat.
Now the rest of the acts of Baasha, and what he did, and his might, are they not written in the book of the chronicles of the kings of Israel?
So Baasha slept with his fathers, and was buried in Tirzah: and Elah his son reigned in his stead.

And also by the hand of the prophet Jehu the son of Hanani came the word of the Lord against Baasha, and against his house, even for all the evil that he did in the sight of the Lord, in provoking him to anger with the work of his hands, in being like the house of Jeroboam; and because he killed him.
In the twenty and sixth year of Asa king of Judah began Elah the son of Baasha to reign over Israel in Tirzah, two years.
And his servant Zimri, captain of half his chariots, conspired against him, as he was in Tirzah, drinking himself drunk in the house of Arza steward of his house in Tirzah.
And Zimri went in and smote him, and killed him, in the twenty and seventh year of Asa king of Judah, and reigned in his stead.

And it came to pass, when he began to reign, as soon as he sat on his throne, that he slew all the house of Baasha: he left him not one that pisseth against a wall, neither of his kinsfolks, nor of his friends.
Thus did Zimri destroy all the house of Baasha, according to the word of the Lord, which he spake against Baasha by Jehu the prophet,
For all the sins of Baasha, and the sins of Elah his son, by which they sinned, and by which they made Israel to sin, in provoking the Lord God of Israel to anger with their vanities.
And Nadab the son of Jeroboam began to reign over Israel in the second year of Asa king of Judah, and reigned over Israel two years.
And he did evil in the sight of the Lord, and walked in the way of his father, and in his sin wherewith he made Israel to sin.

And Baasha king of Israel went up against Judah, and built Ramah, that he might not suffer any to go out or come in to Asa king of Judah.
Then Asa brought out silver and gold out of the treasures of the house of the Lord and of the king’s house, and sent to Ben–hadad king of Syria, that dwelt at Damascus, saying,

There is a league between me and thee, as there was between my father and thy father: behold, I have sent thee silver and gold; go, break thy league with Baasha king of Israel, that he may depart from me.
And Ben–hadad hearkened unto king Asa, and sent the captains of his armies against the cities of Israel; and they smote Ijon, and Dan, and Abel–maim, and all the store cities of Naphtali.
And it came to pass, when Baasha heard it, that he left off building of Ramah, and let his work cease.

They provoked him to jealousy with strange gods, with abominations provoked they him to anger.
They sacrificed unto devils, not to God; to gods whom they knew not, to new gods that came newly up, whom your fathers feared not.
Of the Rock that begat thee thou art unmindful, and hast forgotten God that formed thee.
And when the Lord saw it, he abhorred them, because of the provoking of his sons, and of his daughters.
And he said, I will hide my face from them, I will see what their end shall be: for they are a very froward generation, children in whom is no faith.

They have moved me to jealousy with that which is not God; they have provoked me to anger with their vanities: and I will move them to jealousy with those which are not a people; I will provoke them to anger with a foolish nation.
